one_line: Global AI hardware supply chains tighten amid export curbs, memory shortages, and intensifying geopolitical conflicts over Nvidia and ASML.

themes.title: Export curbs and hardware shortages tighten supply
themes.text: New U.S. export controls have halted server shipments to Southeast Asia and stalled billions in Chinese data center loans. Meanwhile, Nvidia faces S&P downgrade risks, Pentagon scrutiny, and investigations into chip smuggling, while memory shortages drive up hardware prices and extend delivery waits.

stories.headline: Pentagon officials discussed using Defense Production Act over Nvidia CEO role
S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance risks
Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian countries
Nvidia faces ongoing investigations over Megaspeed chip smuggling after CEO’s return
Netherlands seeks to block US MATCH Act restricting ASML China sales
US chip curbs stall billions in data center loans tied to Chinese firms
NVIDIA B300 AI chip orders face up to 40‑week wait; RTX 60 GPU may slip past 2027
Memory chip shortages spark global procurement war rooms and 10x price hikes

themes.title: Legal challenges target chatbot data and toys
themes.text: Forty-two state attorneys general asked a bankruptcy court to block Character.ai's proposed auction of private user chats, and New York became the second state to enact a five-year ban on AI chatbot toys.

stories.headline: 42 state attorneys general challenge Character.ai plan to auction private chats
New York governor signs five-year ban on AI chatbot toys

themes.title: Security risks emerge from labs and hacks
themes.text: Computer scientist Scott Aaronson warned that leading AI labs may hold unreleased cryptographic breakthroughs, while state-backed hackers integrated the Artex penetration tool and confidential data sent to MiniMax was accessed by unknown parties.

stories.headline: AI labs may hold unreleased breakthroughs that could break current cryptosystems
China and North Korean state-backed hackers add AI tool Artex to their arsenals
Confidential data sent to Chinese AI startup MiniMax accessed by unknown parties
